[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Software Supply Chain Security — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to verify that software components and build artifacts resolved during a build process are cryptographically identical to their declared originals — detecting tampering or substitution in the software supply chain.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to verify cryptographic hashes of resolved dependencies against declared manifests or lock files
- Detection of dependency substitution attacks (a dependency resolved with a different hash than previously approved)
- Build artifact signing to enable downstream consumers to verify artifact integrity

**Out of Scope**:
- Vulnerability assessment of dependencies (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10)
- SBOM generation and component inventory (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SBOM-2.7.23)
- Container image integrity verification (addressed partially in GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IMGSC-2.7.13)
- Security controls, configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- Dependency resolution during builds SHALL be pinned to specific, cryptographically verifiable versions; floating version ranges that could resolve to an attacker-substituted version SHALL NOT be used in production builds.
- Build artifacts SHALL be signed after successful build and verification; consumers SHOULD verify signatures before use.
- Any dependency hash mismatch SHALL cause the build to fail; hash mismatches SHALL NOT be silently resolved by re-fetching.
- Signing keys for build artifact attestation SHALL be managed through GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#hash-verification]

#### Hash Verification

**Architectural intent**: Ensure that every component resolved during a build is byte-for-byte identical to its declared version.

**Design guidance**:
- Build pipelines SHALL use lock files or equivalent mechanisms that record the cryptographic hash of every dependency at the version in use.
- Dependency resolution SHALL verify the hash of each resolved component against the lock file; verification failures SHALL abort the build.
- Hash verification SHALL cover both direct and transitive dependencies.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#artifact-signing]

#### Artifact Signing

**Architectural intent**: Provide downstream consumers — including deployment pipelines and admission controllers — with a mechanism to verify that a build artifact was produced by an authorized, verified build process.

**Design guidance**:
- Build artifacts (container images, deployment packages) SHALL be signed using a build pipeline identity.
- Signatures SHOULD be stored as attestations associated with the artifact in the artifact registry.
- The signing process SHOULD occur only after all integrity checks (including hash verification) have passed.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lock File | Inbound | Source Repository | Dependency hash manifest consumed for verification |
| Resolved Dependencies | Inbound | Package Registry / Artifact Store | Components fetched for hash comparison |
| Signing Key | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21 | Artifact signing key retrieved for build attestation |
| Signed Artifact | Outbound | Artifact Registry / GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IMGSC-2.7.13 | Signed artifact with integrity attestation |

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

Dependency Integrity Verification advances the Applications and Workloads pillar by ensuring that the provenance of every component in a workload can be verified — operationalizing the Zero Trust principle that workload identity and composition must be attested, not assumed.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the SA (System and Services Acquisition) family — specifically supply chain integrity and software provenance — and the SI (System and Information Integrity) family's intent for protection against tampered software.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- Lock file-based verification requires discipline in lock file maintenance; lock files that are not committed to version control or are frequently regenerated reduce the effectiveness of this ABB.
- Artifact signing key management depends on GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-VAULT-2.7.21.
- This ABB is complementary to GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SBOM-2.7.23 — integrity verification ensures the components are what they claim to be; SBOM documents what those components are.
